findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing or unreadable file
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or absent file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and use ? on fs::read_to_string

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or missing second field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line panics instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use .map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(e.to_string())) on parse and return Result

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] access Vec indices without bounds checking
findings.failure_mode: empty or short lines panic via IndexOut ofBounds instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) with .ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or restructure with split_once

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy cast from u32 that silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: out-of-range values wrap silently producing incorrect domain data
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) instead of as u16

findings.problem: load_frames fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println), parsing, and domain construction into one function
findings.failure_mode: side-effectful I/O and stdout mutation contaminate pure domain logic; core cannot be tested or reused without triggering real filesystem access
findings.fix: split into shell fn load_frames(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> { parse_records(&fs::read_to_string(path)?); } and pure fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) emits side-effectful stdout inside data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: hidden I/O pollutes output, breaks deterministic testing, and leaks implementation details into the domain layer
findings.fix: remove println entirely; if instrumentation is needed, pass a callback or return metadata separately from the domain records

findings.problem: raw String name and u16 value fields are constructed directly from parsed primitives with no smart constructor or boundary validation
findings.failure_mode: raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.fix: introduce a ParseError enum (Empty, Invalid, Overflow) and a smart constructor Record::new(name: &str, value_str: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> that validates and builds

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates an intermediate Vec<String> instead of using mandated split_once for one-separator grammar
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line; split_once is mandatory for single-separator CSV grammars per Holzman rules
findings.fix: use let (name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; and parse value_str directly

findings.problem: Record uses raw String for name with no newtype, enum, or domain constraint
findings.failure_mode: empty strings, whitespace-only names, or reserved names cannot be rejected at the type level
findings.fix: introduce Name newtype with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and bounded length

residual_risk: This is a static review only with no commands executed. The crate contains 9 blockers: unwrap on I/O and parse, unchecked indexing, lossy as-cast, hidden println I/O, fused shell/core boundaries, missing split_once, absent typed error taxonomy, missing smart constructor/parse boundary, and raw String without newtype. Every absolute law violation is unmitigated. The code will panic on any malformed input, missing file, or value over 65535.
